problem: Rewrite the expression $({x}^{2}-22x+121)-4$ as the difference between a perfect square and a constant.

feedback.problem: Rewrite the expression $({y}^{2}-6y+{3}^{2})+6$ as the sum of a perfect square and a constant.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{y}^{2}-2ay+{a}^{2}=(y-a{)}^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-6y+{3}^{2} & = \\ {y}^{2}-2\cdot 3y+{3}^{2} & = \\ (y-3{)}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}^{2}-6y+{3}^{2})+6 & = \\ (y-3{)}^{2}+6 & .\end{aligned}
$$
